verdict.rationale: C++ is documented as deeply integrated with full engine access and compiles via Visual Studio/XCode (implying full IDE debugger support), and Blueprint visual scripting is documented as exposing 'virtually the full range' of programmer tools. However, community evidence indicates Blueprints alone do not fully expose the API for complex tasks and require dropping to C++ ('blueprints are great for prototyping... once you have too much complexity... use C++'; 'no scripting support... Blueprints are not sufficient'), and C++ is criticized as a barrier ('my main problem with UE is C++'). No single 'primary' scripting language cleanly satisfies all three criteria (productive + full API + debugger) without caveats. Missing for 10: dedicated documentation of a standalone debugger for Blueprint scripting, and stronger evidence that one language alone (without falling back to the other) is both productive and fully API-complete.
